guided.note: Issue #64's guided-discovery axis, from TestGuidedSweepAgainstFloci (go test -run TestGuidedSweepAgainstFloci, TF_FLOCI_TEST=1). cold_calls is the estate-wide sweep's API call count over sweep_types with Request.Guided false; guided_routine_calls is the same sweep with Request.Guided true and a fresh record-store hint (aws_sns_topic present, aws_kms_key and aws_route53_zone absent); guided_verify_calls adds Request.GuidedVerify, which must match cold_calls exactly. The config-driven scan costs nothing in any of the three numbers -- aws_s3_bucket is client-named and never reaches Discover's list/bind machinery, see assertBucketsCostNothing -- so every call counted here belongs to the sweep alone. This is not a ratchet: TestGuidedSweepAgainstFloci's own assertions (guided_routine_calls < cold_calls, guided_verify_calls == cold_calls) are the gate; this section only keeps the artifact's numbers current with the most recent measurement.

note: Issue #64's committed call-count budget. Generated by internal/live/discovery.TestPlanCallBudgetAgainstFloci (go test -run TestPlanCallBudgetAgainstFloci, TF_FLOCI_TEST=1), which reads this file back and fails if a fresh measurement at the same n falls outside the band [calls_total * (1 - floor_tolerance), calls_total * (1 + tolerance)]. The ratchet is two-sided as of issue #630, and the two bounds are separate fields because they guard different things. tolerance is the cost gate: a plan that got more expensive is what a user feels. floor_tolerance is the instrument gate: a one-directional ratchet cannot tell 'we got faster' from 'we stopped measuring something', and this repository has shipped green on the second twice - a cohort that passed because its failing resources vanished from the fixture (#556), and a board row that read pass from a run that measured nothing (#413/#414). Do not collapse the two fields back into one symmetric tolerance on the grounds that they currently hold the same number; they are sized by unrelated arguments, and the floor's is spelled out below. calls_total covers discovery.Discover plus projection.BuildFrom for an N=200 aws_s3_bucket estate (tools/estate-gen -count 200) with no prior state - the read cost live-plan pays end to end, not just the discovery/list half. wall_clock_bucket and measured_at are informational only, never gated: floci's performance on whatever machine runs the test, not this repository's code, is what a wall-clock assertion would actually be grading. calls_by_api's per-bucket shape (22 calls/instance: 3 HEAD /{bucket} plus one GET per S3 subresource the aws_s3_bucket Read covers - acl, cors, encryption, lifecycle, logging, object-lock, policy, replication, requestPayment, versioning, website, accelerate - plus 2 more folded into 'GET /{bucket}/...', which is this proxy's catch-all for any deeper-path or S3-Control-routed call such as bucket tags, plus the 5 the parent-read leg adds per bucket, below) is a property of the AWS provider's own aws_s3_bucket Read and of this fork's parent-read sweep, not of anything else; it is recorded here as the baseline this ratchet protects, not as a target to optimize down. This artifact's second measurement (2026-08-13, merging issue #60's parent-read sweep on top of issue #64's own baseline) adds four new per-bucket GETs the first measurement did not pay: encryption, lifecycle, policy and versioning each double from one GET (the aws_s3_bucket Read's own subresource fetch) to two (a second, independent list of the matching aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration / aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration / aws_s3_bucket_policy / aws_s3_bucket_versioning parent-read child), and publicAccessBlock appears for the first time at one per bucket (aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block has no Read-time analog on aws_s3_bucket itself, only the parent-read child) - the same untaggable-child-via-parent-read discovery issue #60 adds, at the O(N) cost the leg is supposed to pay once the accidental O(N^2) an initial merge of that leg carried (internal/live/discovery/parent_read.go's per-parent unscoped-list loop, fixed the same day) is corrected. See internal/live/discovery/scale_bench_test.go's doc comment for the full method, and internal/live/cloudcontrol/doc.go's 'Retries' section for the backoff policy issue #64 asked for. This artifact's scope was checked again on 2026-08-21, when GitHub issue #349's root-output data-read class added a fourth kind of pre-plan cloud call (one ReadDataSource per data BLOCK a root-level output block reaches, shared across that block's instances, best-effort and never retried): it does not move calls_total, and it is not silently outside the ratchet either. Two independent reasons, both checked rather than assumed. First, TestPlanCallBudgetAgainstFloci counts what discovery.Discover and projection.BuildFrom send, and the new phase runs in the command layer (internal/command/live_plan.go's statelessRootOutputDataReads) beside them, not inside either. Second, and the reason widening the measurement would still read 0: the estate this ratchet is measured over is generated by tools/estate-gen, which emits no root-level output blocks at all, so the phase's demand walk finds nothing to read. An estate whose outputs DO reach data sources pays one call per such block, once, on top of the per-instance read cost above - the same price stock OpenTofu pays for the same blocks on every plan. This artifact's third measurement (2026-08-30, issue #563, re-run at the current pin ghcr.io/lex00/floci@sha256:c55d74e1... after several pin moves this artifact had fallen behind - see live/flociimage_test.go's staleFlociMeasurements) found the per-bucket shape and its 22-call/instance slope completely unchanged, and recorded calls_total = 22*N + 13 at N=20/200/1000. Its reading of the 13-call constant term was wrong, and issue #630 is the correction. This artifact's fourth measurement (2026-08-31 UTC, issue #630, same pin, base commit 4c434c45b2) records calls_total = 4408, down 5 from 4413. The slope is untouched: the fit is now calls_total = 22*N + 8, exact with no residual at all three sizes - N=20: 448, N=200: 4408, N=1000: 22008 (TestScaleAgainstFloci at ESTATE_BENCH_N=20 and 1000 alongside this file's own N=200). What moved is the constant term alone, 13 to 8, and it moved because of issue #627's parent-read guard. The correction to the third measurement's note, which matters because the note is what the next reader extends: it described DescribeRepositories, ListSecrets and 'GET /{bucket}' as 'account/service-level probes that fire once regardless of N'. They are neither probes nor account-level. Every call in this artifact's constant term above ListBuckets is one of parentReadSweep's unscoped child-type list calls (parent_read.go's listUnscopedChildren) - the same leg the second-measurement paragraph above describes as adding four doubled per-bucket GETs. The constant term recorded here and the parent-read residual issue #627 measured on the terralith are the same object, described twice in two files with neither aware of the other; this paragraph is the cross-reference that was missing. Measured rather than assumed, by instrumenting parentReadSweepType: eleven types reach it in this estate. Five are bucket-parented and unscoped with 200 candidate parents each - aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration, aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration, aws_s3_bucket_policy, aws_s3_bucket_versioning and aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block - and those still list; they are the leg's O(N) part and the 5 per-bucket calls in the 22. Five more are unscoped with ZERO candidate parents, because this estate declares nothing but buckets: aws_ecr_repository_policy (DescribeRepositories), aws_sqs_queue_policy (ListQueues), aws_sns_topic_policy (ListTopics), aws_secretsmanager_secret_policy (ListSecrets), and aws_prometheus_scraper_logging_configuration, whose list the counting proxy names 'GET /{bucket}'. That last label is a false friend and is why issue #630 was filed naming four calls when there are five: flocitest.actionOf falls back to path depth when a request carries no X-Amz-Target, no Action form field and no query string, so any single-segment REST GET is reported as 'GET /{bucket}'. This one is an Amazon Managed Prometheus list, not an S3 call. The eleventh type, aws_s3files_file_system_policy, is scoped, so its call always sat inside the per-candidate loop and it never paid anything here either way. Issue #627 skips the unscoped list when the candidate set is empty, so all five zero-candidate calls are gone. Confirmed by controlled revert rather than by subtraction: restoring the pre-#627 ordering reproduces 4413 exactly, with all five keys back. The 8 that remain are 6 'GET ?bucket-region&max-buckets&x-id' (ListBuckets - five from the surviving unscoped bucket-child lists, one from the provider's own account and region resolution) plus GetCallerIdentity and GetUser. Read against issue #546's O(types)-not-O(resources) claim, the share argument the third measurement made still holds and is now stronger against a smaller constant: 8/448 = 1.8% of the total at N=20, 8/22008 = 0.04% at N=1000. floor_tolerance is 0.2, and it is not 0.2 because tolerance is. It is sized off the smallest leg this benchmark pays for, so that a leg going silent cannot pass. At N=200 the 4408 calls are two legs plus three fixed calls: projection's per-instance read (3400, 17 per instance) and the parent-read sweep (1005 - five unscoped lists, each one ListBuckets plus one subresource GET per bucket). The parent-read leg is 22.8% of the total, so a 20% floor is the loosest one that still fails when that whole leg stops running, and a floor much looser than that would let a leg vanish in silence. Proved by measurement, not arithmetic: with parentReadSweep returning immediately the run measures 3403 - which is exactly the pre-parent-read figure this artifact recorded on 2026-08-13 - against a floor of 3526, and the ratchet fails. The margin is thin on purpose. What the floor deliberately does NOT catch is small drift, including the drift that prompted issue #630: this artifact carried 4413 for a day while the code had moved to 4408, which is 0.11% and inside any band anyone would set. Nothing but re-measurement catches that, and pretending otherwise would be worse than saying so. The two guards that do bear on it are live/flociimage_test.go's TestFlociMeasurementsMatchThePinOrSayWhyNot, which forces a re-measurement or a recorded exception whenever the emulator pin moves, and the ordinary discipline of re-measuring in the same change that moves the number. The floor is the collapse detector; it is not the staleness detector. The same round re-ran TestGuidedSweepAgainstFloci, which rewrites the guided section below, and found it stale in the same direction and for the same reason: cold_calls 41 to 37, guided_routine_calls 38 to 32, guided_verify_calls 41 to 37, the sweep no longer paying for parent-read lists of types the guided estate owns no parent of. That section is deliberately not a ratchet - TestGuidedSweepAgainstFloci asserts the relations between its own three numbers, which held before and after - so nothing was wrong there, but it is worth recording that both halves of this file had drifted from the code and only one of them had a gate that could ever have said so.
wall_clock_bucket: single digit to tens of seconds depending on N (this measurement, at commit 4c434c45b2: apply 1.8s / plan 0.3s at N=20, apply 3.3s / plan 1.8s at N=200, apply 18.3s / plan 9.8s at N=1000, measured locally against floci on the machine that recorded this artifact)
